doc.title: Horn Shirley — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Billy Hart as a teenager hanging around the clubs
summary: She met fourteen-year-old Billy Hart, who admired drummer Stump Saunders, and he joined at seventeen.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: To move back to Steeplechase, and actually before that I want to talk to you a bit about Billy Hart. Now, I understand he apprenticed in your ensemble at seventeen.

Yeah. You know, I met Billy, Billy was about fourteen years old and he used to come around the clubs. He loved the drummer that was actually my famous drummer in all the world. He name was Stump Saunders, and he passed a couple of years ago. But he loved Stump, and he loved what we were doing. He‘d come and we were working someplace way up 14th Street, and the man who ran the place was a drummer, and he got to know and like Billy. He let him come in and he‘d sit back behind the stage and listen to Stump. Yeah, he was about fourteen years old, a sweet little guy, bashful and shy. And he was seventeen, and the first time we went on the road his mother said—she was standing on the front porch—―Take care of my baby.‖ Wait a minute. I‘m not going to take care . . . I‘m a few years older than Billy, but not that. [laughs] We had a lot of fun together, yeah, Billy.
How long was he in your ensemble?
You know, I don‘t remember, darling. Okay . . .
Actually, you clarified the first one who . . .
